note: The bands the Tiger Moth plant has to land in, from docs/TIGERMOTH-STAGE1.md, which derives each from Great Planes' Tiger Moth ARF (GPMA1330, the instruction manual's span, area, weight, CG, throws and gear), de Havilland's DH.82A rigging diagram at the kit's 1/4.96, the Ugly Stik's O.S. 61FX on APC's 12 x 6 and the biplane solver the Pitts's derivation uses (scripts/tigermoth-derive.js prints the derived figures). Set from the derivation before the plant was flown. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

t1_level_75.source: level speed at three quarter throttle, the trim, derived 14.41; the band 15 percent either side, the Edge's and the Stik's

t2_stall.source: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax) on the cell's CLmax, each wing's 1.05 over the top wing's bip_r 1.1087, derived 9.47; alphaStall is the cell's angle at which the top wing reaches its CL max, 1.05 / (1.1087 x 4.6328); the band the Edge's in proportion, 6 percent under and 14 over

t3_glide.source: L/D at 1.4 Vs, 13.26 m/s, on the biplane's own induced drag, derived 6.34 (a monoplane of its span and area: 5.92); the band 11 percent either side, the Edge's

t4_top.source: level speed at full throttle, derived 18.69, 10 percent either side

t5_climb.source: the best climb at a held airspeed, full throttle, derived 3.75 m/s at 10.9; 30 percent under and 20 over, the Stik's

t6_roll.source: full aileron on Great Planes' high rate (3/4 in each way on the bottom wing's ailerons alone) from level at the trim, as the helix angle: Clda over -Clp times the throw, derived 0.0962 (88 deg/s at 14.4 m/s); 20 percent either side, the Edge's

t7_adverse.source: from level at the trim, full right aileron with the rudder held centred (the handling notes: 'try full aileron with rudder locked to see adverse yaw'), to 30 deg of bank: on the linear lateral model the nose swings 9.15 deg left, against the roll, and the sideslip peaks at 12.13 deg, 40 percent either side for the estimated K of Nelson's adverse yaw form; with the rudder at three quarters of the aileron with it the sideslip peaks at 0.97 deg and the nose never swings left, held under a third of the rudder locked entry's sideslip and 3 deg the wrong way (at the full rudder it over yaws, 4.3 deg the other way). At 1.3 Vs the same entry is derived 13.09 deg and 17.42 deg, printed, not banded: level at 1.3 Vs needs a throttle the gate cannot hold the speed on without its own hand in the loop

t8_stall_power_off.source: full up held from level at 1.2 Vs with the throttle closed, the wings held on the ailerons as a pilot does, the rudder centred: the top wing, ahead of the CG, stalls first and the nose drops, no wing: no roll rate past 20 deg/s, a wing drop's signature, and under half the aileron on average to hold them, the Stik's U11b bands. 'Stalls, spins, aerobatics are straightforward' (Phillips's handling notes). Its first form, the Stik's U11a, held the ailerons centred too, and read 49 deg of bank after 10 s: at the kit's CG the static margin is 0.038, and full up on the high rate takes both wings deep past their stall, 17 to 24 deg of alpha, where the strips' autorotation grows the left panel's build tolerance into a slow roll off at 10 to 20 deg/s. That run is kept as T8c, recorded and not banded, and is written down in docs/TIGERMOTH-STAGE1.md

t8_stall_power_on.source: the same at half throttle with the wings held on the ailerons, as a pilot does: no roll rate past 20 deg/s, a wing drop's signature, and under half the aileron on average to hold them; the Stik's U11b

t9_phugoid.source: the phugoid at the trim on the linear longitudinal model, derived 13.94 s; 18 percent either side, the Kadet's

t10_prop_torque.source: static full throttle, rolling left: APC's 0.612 N m for the 12 x 6 at 10,895 rpm, the engine's own torque, the Stik's U12

t11_rest.source: the drawn model at rest on its three points: the full size's main axles at 1/4.96 and the kit's 3 1/4 in wheels, the kit's 1 1/4 in tail wheel under the rudder post, derived 8.17 deg nose up, the CG 0.2651 m up and 16.7 percent of the weight on the tail wheel; half a degree, 5 mm and 3.5 points either way, the Pitts's

t12_takeoff.source: the throttle opened over two seconds on grass, the tail held down, then raised, rotated at 1.2 Vs: derived liftoff 14.64 m at 11.36 m/s in 2.3 s; the Pitts's bands in proportion, 27 percent under and 45 over the distance, 15 percent either side of the speed

t13_straight.source: the same take off with the pilot's feet on the rudder and the tail wheel it turns: the manual's 'always be ready to apply right rudder to counteract engine torque'; the Pitts's P13

t14_taxi.source: full right rudder at a walk, the stick a little back to keep the tail wheel down, the throttle whose static thrust is 1.3 times the rolling resistance on grass: the 1.213 m wheelbase over tan of the rudder's 14.59 deg, the tail wheel's wire set in the rudder, derived 4.65 m; the Edge's band in proportion, 21 percent under and 32 over

t15_landing.source: a glide at idle, a flare to the three point attitude, and on the wheels full up held, the manual's 'hold up elevator to place the tail on the ground': at rest on three wheels within 1.5 deg of T11, no hull or prop

t16_unmoved.source: , Re-pinned for the prop's slipstream and its gyroscope on every prop (docs/FLIGHTMODEL.md): the recordings flown under power moved; the five inch's is as it was.

t17_cross_host.source: the Tiger Moth's recorded take off, adverse yaw turn entry, coordinated entry, stall and recovery, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome

t18_idle.source: the engine at O.S.'s 2,000 rpm idle keeps turning and its 1.22 N is under the 3.65 N the grass holds the aircraft with: it stands; the Stik's U19

b1_induced.source: the induced drag factor the plant flies, dCD / d(CL^2) between level at the trim and level at full throttle: Prandtl's biplane form on the lift each wing carries, derived 0.07819 (Munk's span factor 1.137, e 0.85), 5 percent either side, the Pitts's B1; a monoplane of the same span and area, 0.1010, is outside it

b2_linear.source: short of either wing's stall the two wings' lifts sum to the cell's table lift, cl_alpha alpha plus the elevator's cl_de delta_e, within half a percent, the Pitts's B2

b3_top_first.source: a slow pull into the stall, power off: the top wing, ahead and in the bottom wing's bound vortex upwash, carries 1.109 of the cell's CL on its own area and falls short of its linear lift first, its stall blend starting at 9.0 deg of the cell's angle, before the bottom wing's could, at 11.27; and the bottom wing, washed down less by a stalled top wing, gains over its own; the Pitts's B3
